text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.7% today to $154.03, driven by a sharp jump in global oil prices—world crude hit $123.10 per barrel, well above the U.S. price of $103.37. The gap between these two benchmarks, combined with news that Qatari mediators held extensive talks in Tehran aimed at de-escalating U.S.-Iran tensions, suggests markets are pricing in reduced geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Less threat of supply disruptions typically supports crude prices, which benefits major oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock has also benefited from broader strength in energy over the past two weeks (up 5.1%), as refining margins have surged due to tightened fuel supplies—a tailwind for integrated oil companies that both produce crude and refine it into gasoline and diesel. Even as crude prices remain elevated despite Trump's campaign promise to lower gas prices, the actual earnings power of oil majors has improved.
